newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy parliament to pass child-abuse law swiftly.
newsitem.headline: Italy parliament to pass child-abuse law swiftly.

text.p: An 'anti-paedophiles' draft law should be approved by the Italian parliament within weeks, a senior politician said on Thursday with a nation famed for family values in shock over a sudden child-sex scandal.
Centre-left deputy Anna Serafini, vice-president of the lower house Justice commission, said the law was likely to be approved by the commission next week before going to the Senate (upper house).
The measure, which introduces severe punishments for sexual abuse against children, was likely to become law before the end of the summer.

The need for what has been popularly dubbed the "anti-paedophiles law" has been spurred by the arrests in a rundown Naples suburb of Torre Annunziata on Tuesday of 17 people suspected of producing pornographic videos of school children.
This followed a spate of horrific child sex revelations in Belgium and France in recent months.

French authorities have placed more than 300 people under investigation and remanded more than 20 in custody in the last few days in a nationwide inquiry into the sale of pornographic video cassettes involving under-age boys.
The Italian government said on Wednesday it had opened an investigation into the Torre Annunziata affair, which has also shaken confidence in the education system.

"We want to know everything," said Education Minister Luigi Berlinguer, adding that a ministerial enquiry would be carried out alongside one by local magistrates. "We cannot wait even one day because certain crimes cannot be left unpunished."
The minister said he was confident that the episode was a local one and that the Italian education system was sound.
Sventeen people are under preventative detention on suspicion of raping and assaulting 19 children aged between six and nine in Torre Annunziata.
Investigations into the ring began more than a year ago after the mother of one of the children went to the police.
The 17 were also suspected of drugging and chaining up the children while using them to make pornographic videos.
Prosecutor Aldredo Ormanni told reporters this week that some of the children were assaulted at school.
The arrested included several women and a primary school caretaker, who was suspected of helping to lure the children away during recreation time with promises of pocket money.
Newspapers quoted some mothers of children at the school on Thursday as saying that a Mafia-like code of silence had prevented the situation from emerging earlier.
